name: buildkitd
description: BuildKit daemon. gRPC API on `/run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock` (Linux) or `npipe:////./pipe/buildkitd` (Windows). Two worker backends: OCI (runc) and containerd; OCI default. Reads `/etc/buildkit/buildkitd.toml`. Listens on Unix socket by default; can expose TCP via `--addr tcp://...` (use TLS).

name: buildx driver: docker
description: Default `docker buildx` driver. Uses the BuildKit library bundled with dockerd (no external buildkitd). Limited: doesn't support multi-platform, cache exports, or experimental Dockerfile features. Auto-selected when no other driver is configured.

name: buildx driver: docker-container
description: Runs buildkitd inside a container managed by buildx. Most-used driver for advanced features: multi-platform, cache export, custom buildkitd config. Created via `docker buildx create --driver docker-container`.

name: buildx driver: kubernetes
description: Runs buildkitd as a Kubernetes Deployment / StatefulSet — for shared CI builders. Configurable replicas, node selector, rootless mode. `docker buildx create --driver kubernetes`.

name: buildx driver: remote
description: Connects to a pre-existing buildkitd over TCP/socket. Used for shared org-wide builders. e.g. `docker buildx create --driver remote tcp://buildkit.example.com:1234`. Pairs with TLS for production.

name: BuildKit frontend
description: A pluggable component that converts a human-readable build format (e.g. Dockerfile) to LLB. Distributed as container images (`docker/dockerfile:1.6`); user pins a specific version via `# syntax=`. The reason newer Dockerfile features (RUN --mount=, here-docs, etc.) work without upgrading buildkitd.

name: Dockerfile frontend
description: The default frontend that parses Dockerfiles to LLB. Released as `docker/dockerfile` images; latest stable: `docker/dockerfile:1`. Newer features land here first, available to anyone via `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:<version>`.

name: BuildKit LLB
description: Low-Level Build — protobuf-based intermediate format defining a content-addressable dependency graph of build operations. The thing every frontend compiles to. Concurrently executable, efficiently cacheable, vendor-neutral. 'LLB is to Dockerfile what LLVM IR is to C.'

name: Dockerfile stage
description: A `FROM <image> [AS <name>]` block in a Dockerfile. Multi-stage builds chain stages; later stages can `COPY --from=<stage>` from earlier ones. Unused stages are skipped; independent stages run in parallel. Build target via `--target <stage>`.

name: Dockerfile instruction
description: A single line in a Dockerfile (FROM, RUN, COPY, etc.). Each becomes one LLB op (and potentially one image layer for FS-modifying instructions). Order matters — caching is from-the-top, so any change invalidates downstream.

name: build context
description: The directory tree the build sees as `.`. Streamed to buildkitd by buildx (incrementally — only changed files since last build). Filtered by `.dockerignore`. Forms: local path, git URL, URL+ref+subdir, named (additional) context.

name: build arg (ARG)
description: Build-time variable declared with `ARG NAME[=default]`. Pass via `--build-arg NAME=val`. Visible only AFTER the ARG declaration; an ARG before FROM is global. Distinct from ENV — ARG values aren't baked into the resulting image (so secrets via ARG leak via `docker history`).

name: build secret
description: `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=<name>` mounts a secret as a tmpfs file inside the RUN. Source from CLI (`--secret id=<name>,src=<path>` or `,env=<env-var>`). Secret content NEVER ends up in image layers — solves the 'secret in ARG leaks via `docker history`' problem.

name: build SSH mount
description: `RUN --mount=type=ssh` forwards the host's SSH agent socket to a build step. Lets `git clone` private repos without baking the key. CLI: `--ssh default` (uses host SSH agent) or `--ssh <id>=<path-to-key>`.

name: cache mount
description: `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=<path>[,id=<id>][,sharing=shared|private|locked]` reuses a writable directory across builds. Used for package-manager caches (`/root/.cache/go-build`, `/var/cache/apt`). Per-builder; not part of any image layer.

name: tmpfs mount (build)
description: `RUN --mount=type=tmpfs,target=<path>` mounts an in-memory tmpfs for the duration of the RUN. Useful for scratch / disposable temp dirs that mustn't pollute layers.

name: bind mount (build)
description: `RUN --mount=type=bind,source=<context-path>,target=<path>` exposes context-side files into the RUN without making a layer copy. Read-only by default; `,rw` for writable. Replaces COPY for build-only access patterns.

name: output tarball
description: `--output type=docker|oci,dest=<file>.tar` exports the build result as a tarball instead of (or in addition to) loading into the local image store. Forms: `type=image` (default), `type=local,dest=<dir>`, `type=tar,dest=-`, `type=registry`, `type=docker`, `type=oci`.

name: inline cache
description: `--cache-to type=inline` embeds the cache manifest in the pushed image (extra layer with cache metadata). Pull the image to get the cache. Simplest sharing pattern for CI; slightly larger images.

name: registry cache
description: `--cache-to type=registry,ref=<image>,mode=max` pushes the cache as a separate manifest in a registry. `--cache-from type=registry,ref=<image>` pulls it. `mode=max` saves all layers including intermediate; `mode=min` (default) only the final layers.

name: local cache
description: `--cache-to type=local,dest=<path>` writes cache to a local directory. `--cache-from type=local,src=<path>` reads it. Useful when a registry isn't available; caches must be persisted between CI runs (cache action).

name: S3 cache
description: `--cache-to type=s3,region=<>,bucket=<>,prefix=<>,name=<>`. Experimental. Useful when CI is on AWS and you want shared org-wide cache.

name: GitHub Actions cache
description: `--cache-to type=gha,scope=<>,name=<>` writes to GitHub Actions' cache backend (env GITHUB_TOKEN required). Tightly integrated with `actions/cache`. Experimental.

name: Azure Blob cache
description: `--cache-to type=azblob,account_url=<>,account_name=<>,name=<>,prefix=<>`. Azure equivalent of S3 cache. Experimental.

name: OCI cache
description: `--cache-to type=oci,dest=<dir>` writes cache as an OCI layout dir. Used by tools that consume the OCI format directly.

name: FROM
description: `FROM <image>[:<tag>|@<digest>] [AS <stage-name>]`. Sets the base image for the next stage. Multiple FROM = multi-stage. `FROM scratch` = empty rootfs (smallest possible image). Pin to digest for reproducibility.

name: RUN
description: `RUN <command>` (shell form, wraps in /bin/sh -c) or `RUN ["exec","args",...]` (exec form). Creates a new layer with command output. Mounts: `RUN --mount=type=bind|cache|secret|ssh|tmpfs`. Network isolation: `RUN --network=default|none|host`. Privilege: `RUN --security=insecure|sandbox` (insecure requires --allow=security.insecure on build).

name: COPY
description: `COPY [--from=<stage|image>] [--chown=<user:group>] [--chmod=<mode>] [--link] <src> [<src>...] <dest>`. From context (default) or another stage/image. `--link` decouples the copy from previous-layer cache invalidation (faster rebuilds).

name: ADD
description: Like COPY but also supports URL fetch (`ADD https://...`) and tar auto-extract (`.tar.gz` etc.). `--checksum=sha256:<hex>` for integrity check on URL fetch. Generally prefer COPY unless you need ADD's special features.

name: CMD
description: Default args to entrypoint. Forms: `CMD ["executable","arg"]` (exec — preferred), `CMD ["arg"]` (default args to ENTRYPOINT), `CMD command arg` (shell — wraps in /bin/sh -c). Replaced when `docker run <image> <override>`.

name: ENTRYPOINT
description: Binary the container runs. Exec form (`["binary","arg"]`) preferred — signals propagate properly. Shell form wraps in /bin/sh -c (PID 1 = sh, signals don't reach the binary).

name: ENV
description: `ENV KEY=VALUE [KEY=VALUE...]`. Sets env vars in the image AND for subsequent build steps. Persists into the running container. Distinct from ARG.

name: ARG
description: `ARG NAME[=default]`. Build-time variable. Visible after declaration (or globally if before first FROM). Pass via `--build-arg`. Common globals: `BUILDPLATFORM`, `TARGETPLATFORM`, `TARGETOS`, `TARGETARCH`, `TARGETVARIANT` (auto-set in multi-platform builds).

name: LABEL
description: `LABEL key=value [key=value...]`. Adds metadata labels to the image. Standard keys: `org.opencontainers.image.{title,description,authors,vendor,licenses,source,documentation,version,revision,created}`.

name: EXPOSE
description: `EXPOSE <port>[/<proto>]` declares ports the image listens on. Pure metadata — doesn't actually publish. `-P` consumes EXPOSE entries (auto-publishes to ephemeral host ports).

name: VOLUME
description: `VOLUME <path>` declares a path as a volume mount point. At `docker run`, an anonymous volume is auto-created if no `-v`/--mount targets the path. Foot-gun: makes the directory unmodifiable in subsequent layers.

name: USER
description: `USER <uid|name>[:<gid|group>]`. Sets the user for subsequent RUN/CMD/ENTRYPOINT. Hardening best practice: drop to non-root (`USER 1000:1000`) before CMD.

name: WORKDIR
description: `WORKDIR <path>`. Sets cwd for subsequent instructions. Auto-creates if missing.

name: HEALTHCHECK
description: `HEALTHCHECK [OPTIONS] CMD <command>` defines an in-image health probe. Options: `--interval`, `--timeout`, `--retries`, `--start-period`, `--start-interval`. `HEALTHCHECK NONE` clears any inherited check.

name: ONBUILD
description: `ONBUILD <instruction>`. Triggers when a downstream image uses this image as base. Used in language-base images: 'whoever uses me must have a package.json' patterns. Often ill-advised — surprising behavior for downstream users.

name: STOPSIGNAL
description: `STOPSIGNAL <signal>` sets the kill signal for `docker stop` (and the image's StopSignal config field). Default SIGTERM. e.g. nginx uses SIGQUIT for graceful shutdown.

name: SHELL
description: `SHELL ["executable","arg",...]`. Override the shell used for shell-form RUN/CMD/ENTRYPOINT. Default Linux: `["/bin/sh","-c"]`. Common Windows: `["powershell","-Command"]` or `["cmd","/S","/C"]`.

name: multi-stage build
description: Multiple `FROM` blocks; later stages `COPY --from=<earlier-stage>`. Final image only contains what's in the last stage (or `--target=<stage>`). Drastic image size reduction (build tools left in early stage, only the binary copied to the final).

name: cross-platform build
description: `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/arm/v7 .` builds a multi-arch image and pushes a manifest list. Uses QEMU-static for non-native arches OR remote builders. `BUILDPLATFORM` (where it runs), `TARGETPLATFORM` (what it builds for) ARGs auto-injected.

name: parallel stage execution
description: BuildKit runs independent stages concurrently. Final stage waits on its dependencies (`COPY --from=<x>` or `RUN` in stages it depends on). Big speedup for monorepos.

name: shared build cache
description: `--cache-from` + `--cache-to` push/pull cache to a shared backend. CI builds reuse cache across runners. Combined with `mode=max` to save intermediate layers.

name: secrets not in layers
description: `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=token` mounts a secret as a tmpfs file for one RUN. Secret content is NEVER captured in image layers. Solves 'secret leaked via `docker history`' problems caused by --build-arg.

name: heredoc syntax
description: `RUN <<EOF` / `COPY <<EOF` writes inline multi-line content. Supports `<<-EOF` (strip leading tabs), `<<"EOF"` (no-interpolation). Cleaner than `RUN echo "line1" && echo "line2"` chains.

name: --mount=type=cache sharing
description: `RUN --mount=type=cache,id=<id>,sharing=shared|private|locked,target=<path>`. `shared` = concurrent builds share; `private` = each build's own; `locked` = serialize concurrent access. The `id` namespace lets multiple builds share the same package-manager cache safely.

name: bake target matrix
description: `docker buildx bake` uses HCL/JSON/Compose to define a build matrix. `target.<name>` per build target; `group.<name>.targets` for groups; `variable.<name>` for parameterization. CI driver for multi-target / multi-platform builds.

name: build args from env
description: `docker buildx build --build-arg HTTP_PROXY` (no `=`) pulls value from caller's env. Useful for proxy / token passthrough without baking the value into a CI script.

name: .dockerignore patterns
description: `.dockerignore` (in build context root) excludes paths from the context BEFORE upload. Patterns: `*` (any chars in name), `?` (single char), `**` (any nested dirs), `!pattern` (negate), `# comment`. Critical for build perf — without it, `node_modules/`, `.git/`, etc. get streamed every build.

name: # syntax= directive
description: `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` (or :1.6, or @sha256:...) at the top of a Dockerfile. Pins the frontend image. Lets new Dockerfile features land without daemon upgrade. Pin to a specific minor for reproducibility; use :1 to auto-upgrade within v1.

name: parser directive
description: Top-of-file `# directive=value` lines. Three: `# syntax=`, `# escape=`, `# check=`. Must be at the very top — first non-directive line ends parser-directive parsing.

name: here-document
description: YAML/shell-style multi-line literal: `<<EOF ... EOF`. Inside a Dockerfile RUN/COPY: provides the content of a file or multi-line script. Variants: `<<-EOF` (strip leading tabs), `<<"EOF"` (literal — no var interpolation).

name: cache key derivation
description: BuildKit derives a cache key per LLB op from: the op type, its args, the SHA of any input mounts, and the SHA of mount sources. Change any input → new cache key → re-execution. The reason `COPY package.json` before `RUN npm install` makes npm install cacheable across most builds.

name: layer deduplication
description: Same layer (by content-addressable digest) is stored once on disk regardless of how many images reference it. Engine + registry both dedupe. The reason 100 images sharing `ubuntu:24.04` only cost the layer's size once.

name: ENTRYPOINT/CMD shell vs exec form
description: Exec form (`["binary","arg"]`) execs directly — pid 1 IS the binary, signals propagate. Shell form (`binary arg`) wraps in /bin/sh -c — pid 1 is sh, your binary is sh's child, SIGTERM goes to sh and is dropped. Always prefer exec form for production.

name: shell vs exec form (rules)
description: Shell form: arguments are a single string passed to /bin/sh -c. Exec form: JSON array, NO shell — env vars NOT expanded by shell, signals direct. Mix-up causes 'why doesn't $HOME expand?' on exec-form RUN.

name: image tag vs digest
description: `FROM nginx:1.27` (mutable) vs `FROM nginx@sha256:...` (immutable). For reproducible builds, pin to digest. CI updates the pin on a schedule (renovate / dependabot) so security patches still land.

name: OCI vs docker v2-2 image format
description: Two manifest formats, mostly compatible. BuildKit defaults to OCI; legacy builder used Docker v2-2. Cross-references in `docker.runtime.media-type`. Some old registries reject OCI-only manifests; force docker format with `--provenance=false --output type=docker`.

name: frontend image pinning
description: `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.6.0` pins to an exact frontend version. Reproducibility + new-feature gating. Trade-off: pin-too-tight = miss security fixes; pin-too-loose = nondeterministic builds.

name: experimental Dockerfile syntax
description: `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1-labs` opts into experimental features (new instruction forms, mount types). Lands in `:1` mainline once stable.

name: Dockerfile comment
description: Lines starting with `#` (and not matching parser directive form) are comments. `#` mid-line isn't a comment — only at start. Backslash continuations (`\`) work for multi-line instructions.

name: # escape= directive
description: Top-of-file `# escape=\\` (default) or `# escape=`` ` ``. Sets the line-continuation character for the rest of the Dockerfile. Use backtick for Windows where backslash is path separator.
